title: src/models/: how the order-2 model's counts adapt (a rate that slows as evidence grows)
context: One idea: how the order-2 model's count adapts. Today each count of 16 bits moves a sixteenth of the way towards each bit (RATE 4), whatever it has seen. Let it adapt faster while a context is new and slower as evidence grows (a small counter kept with the count), or keep two speeds at once and give both as predictions. Work in the order-2 file of src/models/ (new, predict, update). The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least one percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. Today the total is 4,890,484 bytes, the message 3,544,012 and the program 1,346,472; a count's extra state must not cost more memory than the bound allows. The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB. The first tip takes about 0.35 s to encode and 0.83 s to decode and 47 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.

title: src/refine.rs: correct the mixed probability by what came true in a small context
context: Make the refining step learn. Today Refine::refine returns its input and Refine::update learns nothing. Correct the mixed probability by what came true in a small context: bucket the probability, choose a bucket by the bits of the current byte known so far or by the last byte, keep for each bucket a probability that moves towards the bits seen, and blend it with the input. The judge measures the tip and your candidate in the same judgement: the goal is a total_bytes (the message plus the program as built) at least half a percent lower than the tip's, confirmed by sure_total_bytes beyond the noise. A candidate that is right but no smaller meets no goal. It pays more once the mixer learns and two or three models are in; today the total is 4,890,484 bytes, the message 3,544,012 and the program 1,346,472. Work in src/refine.rs (new, refine, update). The program must bring the corpus back from its message alone, byte for byte, and nothing outside src/ may change. Stay under six tenths of the bounds: 54 seconds of processor time a phase and 1,600 MB. The first tip takes about 0.35 s to encode and 0.83 s to decode and 47 MB; run bee/check 0 before and after your change to scale what you see on your machine.

title: src/context.rs and src/models/: a hash of the word so far, and a word model that reads it
context: Give every model one more thing to look at, and use it in one model: a word model. Add to the context what the frame keeps (a hash of the word being written so far, updated in Context::push when a byte is a letter or an apostrophe, else reset), then a new model file in src/models/ that chooses its count by that hash and the bits of the byte known so far. The new field has no gain by itself, so the field and the model that reads it are one task. title: src/frame.rs: two passes, measure first then code with what was learnt
context: One idea: two passes in the frame. Measure the data first, then code it with what was learnt (for example which of a few settings of the model is best), the choice written in the message.
